quality.s1.title: S1 — position extraction against the team lead's gold
quality.s1.draw: a draw of {drawn} rows from a population of {population}, seed {seed}
quality.s1.absent: the gold is not labelled yet
quality.s1.limits: Where the loss sits: the product field carries free text where the law asks for the printed line or the category; brand surface forms drift; one small-print grid page is misread wholesale. The bar is published as measured — nothing was loosened
quality.s2.title: S2 — reactions under promo posts
quality.ties.title: The codebook's ties
quality.limits.title: The limits, said out loud
quality.limits.body: Every number on these screens is a field of a named file. Empty means one of three things — not collected, not exported, none in the data — and the screen says which
loop.question: What did the loop do last, and when will it run again?
loop.tick.title: The last tick
loop.windows.title: Windows
loop.queue.title: The queue
loop.money.title: The cycle's budget
loop.money.display_only: a display value, not a budget: this is the guard's last RECORDED line and not a balance call
loop.schedule.title: Schedule
loop.schedule.rule: the default interval may not be below the minimum, and the minimum may not be below an hour
loop.schedule.readonly: a static build has no API — the schedule is read-only
loop.schedule.not_in_build: the intervals live in data/schedule.json — the daemon's file, which a static build does not carry
loop.tick.no_api: a static build has no API — the tick cannot be run from here
loop.paid.never: the loop buys nothing: the paid reading of the queue is the operator's word, and this process has no entry point to it
week.rule: the reporting week is the newest ISO week ANY chain has leaflet pages in: {chains} of {total} chains carry a set in it, the rest are shown on their own newest week, and no row of theirs is folded into another week’s aggregate
week.older: an earlier week than the reported one
media.fresh.rule: one card per chain — the newest week that chain has pages in
media.none: no page joined the media records
media.rows_without_a_page: without a photo: {rows} of {total} — no media record carries an image for those posts
trends.prices.subtitle: for the current week; the median leads, the cheapest and the dearest come with their page
trends.prices.rule: the price of a kilogram or a litre comes from the promo price and the size of that same row, divided by the pieces in the pack; a category is read per unit, because a median over grams and millilitres would be a sum with no unit
trends.prices.without: without a price per unit: {rows} — the row carries no price or no size
trends.prices.count: positions with a price per unit: {priced} of {positions}
trends.prices.group_hint: the rows whose subcategory was not printed — not the whole group
region.chain.no_pages: this chain has no leaflet in the data — its positions were not read off pages
region.claim: the chains the operator names as present in the oblast — a selection of CHAINS, not a geography of rows: the registry carries no region and no city, and the leaflets of the national chains are national. Each chain is shown on its own newest week with leaflets
trends.prices.excluded: excluded {rows}: the page prints no price
prices.corrected: corrected by hand against the leaflet page
trends.conclusions.title: Three readings of the week
trends.conclusions.rule: the readings are generated by fixed code rules from the export's figures — no free prose from a model; each rule names what it compared before it names what it found. Below are the fields this reading stands on
trends.exhibit.week: reporting week {week} · rows are each chain's own current week
trends.exhibit.untitled: no rule found a reading for this exhibit
trends.spread.subtitle: from the cheapest to the dearest position in each category × unit pair; the dot is the median
trends.spread.rule: the axis is shared inside one unit and never across two: UAH/kg and UAH/L on one scale would invite a comparison of a kilogram with a litre
trends.ranking.subtitle: a channel's median inside one category
trends.ranking.rule: the median is cut inside one category and one unit — a chain's median over everything it sells would read the chain with more cheese on its leaflet as the expensive one; the number of positions stands beside every bar, because one row is also a median
trends.ranking.channels: a row is a collected channel, not a retailer: one retailer reaches this ranking through several of them, and an aggregator channel reprints another chain's leaflet, so the same offer can stand in more than one bar
trends.ranking.market: the dashed line is the category's market median: {value}
cc.info.absent: the dictionary carries no definition for this metric
cc.unknown.title: no such tab
cc.unknown.body: the address {path} names no command-centre tab

cc.t7.question: When should an alert fire?
cc.t7.population: one window is a point; there is no baseline
cc.t7.preview: The rule as it will be
cc.t7.rule.deviation: an alert is a metric's deviation from the previous window's baseline
cc.t7.rule.both: both polarities: a sharp fall and a sharp rise are equally worth a look
cc.t7.rule.threshold: the threshold is the operator's, ruled on the alert design — none is invented here
cc.t7.no_numbers: there is deliberately no figure on this tab: the baseline to compute one against is not collected yet
